question: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q3 FY2027 earnings release? (Gross margin (GAAP))

calls.reasoning: On the Aug 26, 2026 Q2 FY27 call, CFO Kress guided Q3 GM to 74.0% (GAAP=non-GAAP) and said GM would bottom at 71-72% in Q4 FY27 on memory costs, recovering to 72-73% in FY28. NVIDIA historically guides within previously signaled ranges (e.g., 'mid-70s' exit -> 75.0% Q4 FY26 guide), so the midpoint 71.5% is the anchor. Memory prices were said to be rising faster than expected (supply commitments $119B->$279B), giving some downside tilt; Rubin ramp yield/mix could help. GAAP and non-GAAP have been ~equal, so the GAAP figure is close to non-GAAP. Small tail below range for a one-off inventory/charge-driven GAAP guide. Polymarket only prices the Q3 actual non-GAAP GM (73-75% at 0.74, thin volume), which is not this contract.
calls.dossier:
- Q2 FY27 press release (Aug 26, 2026): GAAP GM 75.0%, non-GAAP 75.0%; Q1 FY27 GAAP 74.9%/non-GAAP 75.0%. Q3 FY27 outlook: GAAP and non-GAAP GM 74.0% +/-50bp; revenue $108.0B +/-2%; no China DC compute assumed.
- Q2 call (Aug 26, 2026, per Motley Fool Aug 29 / Dealroom / CNBC / gamesreviews headline): CFO Kress said GM expected to bottom at 71%-72% in Q4 FY27, then stabilize at 72-73% in FY28 as price increases take effect; cause: 'extreme pricing conditions in memory', memory price increases exceeded prior expectations and headed higher into next year.
- Earlier FY27 framing: management targeted holding margins 'in the mid-70s' for FY27; Q4 signal is below that.
- Supply commitments rose from $119B to $279B, primarily memory procurement (TrendForce Aug 27, 2026). NVIDIA announced custom NVHBM.
- 24/7 Wall St (Oct 19, 2026): repeats margin bottoming at 71-72%; Vera Rubin ramp in progress; no new margin guidance update found since August.
- Precedent: Q4 FY26 guide was 75.0% after 'exit in mid-70s' signal; Q1 FY26 GAAP guide 70.6% during Blackwell ramp. NVIDIA typically gives a point midpoint +/-50bp.
- GAAP vs non-GAAP GM recently identical or within ~0.1pp.
- Status quo: guidance is consistent with the pre-signaled 71-72% bottom.
- Resolves off GAAP GM midpoint in 'Outlook' section of the Q3 FY27 press release (expected ~Nov 2026), not non-GAAP and not the actual Q3 result.
- Event window: Q3 FY27 release date (around Nov 18-19, 2026) -> per criteria; as of Oct 19, 2026, release not yet published.
- Searched, not found: any intra-quarter margin update from NVIDIA since Aug 26; analyst consensus for the Q4 GM guide; a market on the Q4 guide itself (Polymarket only covers the Q3 actual non-GAAP GM).

calls.reasoning: On the Aug 26, 2026 Q2 FY27 call, CFO Kress said gross margin would bottom at 71-72% in Q4 FY27 because of memory costs, then recover to 72-73% in FY28. Q3 was guided at 74.0% +/-50bp, with GAAP equal to non-GAAP. NVIDIA usually gives a point estimate +/-50bp and keeps it inside ranges it has already signalled, so the midpoint of 71.5% is the anchor. Memory prices rising faster than expected pull the estimate down. Price increases, Rubin product mix and the habit of guiding conservatively pull it up. These roughly cancel, with fat edges at 71.0 and 72.0. A one-off charge driving GAAP below 68.95% is a small tail.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs report the same facts: the 71-72% Q4 trough signal, the 74.0% Q3 guide, GAAP equal to non-GAAP recently, and no update since August. None of the runs found a market that matches this contract. The Polymarket listings price the Q3 actual non-GAAP margin, with the 73-75% bucket at 0.74 on thin volume. That is consistent with the 74% Q3 guide but is not an anchor here. The only differences between the runs are small judgment calls on tail width and skew. I keep the 71.5% median the evidence supports, with a 1.4pp 10-90 width. That sits between the runs' widths and reflects real ambiguity between 71.0, 71.5 and 72.0 point guides, plus some memory-cost downside. I retrieved nothing new on this run.

disagreements.verdict: Set at 1.4pp. The pre-signalled band is tight, but further memory cost increases and the choice between 71.0, 71.5 and 72.0 point guides justify modest tails.

disagreements.claim: Direction of tail risk (below-range vs above-range escape)
disagreements.verdict: Downside escape kept at 2%, because a GAAP-only charge or a memory shock could plausibly push the figure below 68.95. No concrete mechanism takes the guide above 73.05, so no upside escape is declared.
